Anthropic Colossus 1 (220k+ GPU) compute lock-in from May 6 still anchors the upside scenario for 2027–28 declarations. Resolution window now ~30 months. Hold; capability bullish, declaration friction higher.

forecasts.question: Will economic consultancy lose ≥33% value/jobs by end 2030 due to AI?
forecasts.key_change: Up 1pp to 23%. Industry coverage in the past 24 hours continues to confirm structural pressure: McKinsey ~10% non-client cuts, BCG growing only via AI/tech specialists rather than generalists, Bain/Deloitte/KPMG/Accenture all in cut mode in 2025–26. The May 4 OpenAI ($4B Deployment Co) and Anthropic ($1.5B JV) consulting ventures remain the structural marker. With ~4.5 years to deadline and the demand-side delivery model now actively contested by capitalised AI-native entrants, drift continues upward. Still well below 50% — incumbents have margins to absorb AI as augmentation rather than substitution and revenue erosion to date is concentrated in headcount, not topline.

forecasts.question: Will Labour be largest party at next UK General Election?
forecasts.key_change: Down 1pp to 1%. May 7 local elections now substantially declared (~129 of 136 councils): Reform UK +1,428 seats, Labour −1,375, with Sky News National Equivalent Vote at Reform 27%, Conservative 20%, Labour 15%, Green 14%, LD 14%, Independents 10%. Labour is now the third party on national vote share. Farage declared a 'historic shift'; Starmer says he won't step down. Council control: Labour lost 34, Reform gained 13. For Labour to be largest party at the next GE, the electorate would need to swing ~10pp net back to Labour from Reform/Greens AND for Reform's surge to deflate to a sub-25% share — neither is consistent with current trajectory or with the structural Reform-Conservative right that this NEV implies.
forecasts.base_rate: ~5% — incumbents this far behind on NEV (Labour 15%) at locals rarely win the next GE
factors_up: Long horizon to GE (Dec 2029) leaves time for Reform implosion or scandal (+2pp)
First-past-the-post electoral system can reward Labour vote efficiency in fragmented field (+1pp)
Macroeconomic improvement could plausibly lift Labour vote share (+1pp)
factors_down: Sky NEV: Labour 15%, third place behind Reform 27% and Con 20% (-4pp)
Labour lost ~1,375 council seats; Reform gained ~1,428 (-3pp)
Labour lost control of 34 councils; Reform took 13 (-2pp)
Electoral Calculus April MRP still projects Reform+Con coalition (-1pp)
Starmer remaining as leader despite collapse compounds political damage (-1pp)
key_uncertainties: Whether Reform sustains 27% share through 2027–29 or collapses on contact with delivery responsibility
Whether a Labour leadership change shifts the trajectory
Whether tactical anti-Reform voting consolidates around a single non-Reform party

update_triggers.up: Major Reform scandal, leadership crisis or polling collapse below 18%; Labour leadership change with bounce above 25%
update_triggers.down: Reform sustains >28% in averaged polls through Q3 2026; Labour drops below 14% in MRP

forecasts.question: Will China initiate a military blockade or invasion of Taiwan before 1 January 2030?
forecasts.key_change: Hold at 8%. AEI May 8 China-Taiwan update describes continued multi-domain coercion: PLA Navy two major SCS/West-Pacific deployments responding to Balikatan 2026, ongoing blockade rehearsals, expanded coast-guard pressure. None of this represents an inflection toward kinetic action — it remains gradient coercion below the resolution threshold. Allied combined exercises (US/Phil/Japan/Aus/Can) running April 20–May 1 continue to raise the cost of any blockade attempt. With ~44 months remaining and consensus expert view that Beijing is not planning 2027 attack, base rate drift remains downward but the floor is held by ongoing rehearsal and gray-zone escalation risk.

forecasts.key_change: Hold at 1%. The April 2026 ONS CPI release is scheduled for May 21; consensus expects modest dip but remaining well above 2%.
